## Course outline and printable lecture notes {#course-outline}

- I have planned twelve self-contained chapters across thirteen teaching
  weeks, including the opening self-study week, to allow for class
  suspensions and catch-up work. Chapter numbers match the numbered
  teaching weeks.
- If we stay on schedule, we may also discuss introductory automata theory
  and mathematical ways of describing computer programs and their behaviour.
- There are no coding assignments; pseudocode may be used.

## Class format

**Saturday Meeting Timetable**

- **10:30 a.m.–12 noon:** lecture on the current chapter.
- **12 noon–1:00 p.m.:** lunch break.
- **1:00–1:30 p.m.:** recap of the previous chapter.
- **1:30–2:30 p.m.:** problems on the previous chapter.

**Preparation and participation**

- **Read the assigned chapter before class** and attempt the previous
  chapter's problems. You need not have mastered the material; identify
  where you need help. Questions will draw on the reading, with guidance
  as needed.
- **Recitation** is graded at every meeting on the quality of your
  reasoning, rather than how often you speak. There are no traditional quizzes.
- **Consultations:** I am available after class; if nobody approaches
  within five minutes of dismissal, I will leave. You may also email questions.

## Assessment

::: {.discrete-grading-table}

| Component | Weight |
|---|---:|
| Problem sets (best four of five) | 50% |
| Attendance | 5% |
| Recitation | 15% |
| Midterm examination | 15% |
| Final examination | 15% |
| **Total** | **100%** |

:::

- Problem-set scores are converted to percentages. The lowest is dropped;
  the remaining four are averaged, with each retained set accounting for
  **12.5%** of the course mark.
- Term examinations use **zero-based grading**.
- The minimum passing percentage is **75%**, equivalent to **3.00**
  ([Student Manual, Part II, Section K](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ew8hDsW_anZjLsZJKI3rEKAnhT1K4OTd/view)).

### Bonus for Mathematical Corrections {#mathematical-corrections}

- Question my reasoning and raise suspected mistakes.
- Each confirmed significant error in the notes or lectures earns **five
  percentage points on one examination mark** (for example, 70% becomes 75%).
- A significant error affects a claim, calculation or reasoning; harmless
  typographical errors do not qualify.
- I will choose the examination and redirect any credit above 100% to
  other components in whichever way benefits you most.
- Raw marks and bonus adjustments are recorded separately.

### Final examination exemption

To qualify:

- **Pre-final standing:** 1.50 or better.
- **Coursework:** all course requirements completed.
- **Attendance:** perfect attendance, as an additional course condition;
  valid excused absences do not count against this requirement.

The academic conditions follow the
[Student Manual, Part II, Section J.5](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ew8hDsW_anZjLsZJKI3rEKAnhT1K4OTd/view).

Let $P$ be your best-four problem-set average, $A$ your attendance score,
$R$ your recitation score and $M$ your midterm score, all percentages after
any bonus credit. Your pre-final percentage is

$$
S=\frac{50P+5A+15R+15M}{85}.
$$

- Convert $S$ using the University's grading scale to obtain your pre-final
  standing.
- **If exempt and not taking the final:** I will record the exemption and
  use $S$ as the placeholder for its 15% component, preserving your pre-final
  percentage and grade.
- **If exempt and choosing to take the final:** You waive the exemption.
  I will record your actual examination score, including any bonus credit,
  and use it at the usual 15% weight to calculate your course grade, as for
  a student without an exemption. Your final course grade may be better or
  worse than your pre-final standing.

## Problem sets {#problem-sheets}

- **All submissions must be handwritten.**
- Each problem set will allow **at least two weeks** for completion.
- Late or missing submissions receive **zero** unless an accepted excuse
  or university-approved arrangement applies.
- An unexcused absence does not extend a deadline or entitle you to a
  make-up assessment.

**AI and face-to-face checks**

- You may use AI for revision, but not to solve assigned problem sets.
- Examinations and recitations require independent answers without AI.
- I may ask you to explain your submitted solution in person: your approach,
  notation and reasons for particular steps.
- These discussions will not include unrelated or trick questions, or
  require a different solution.
- If you cannot give even a basic account of your own reasoning, the
  problem set receives **zero**.

Problem sets will be posted here when issued.

## Course policies

The approved syllabus and university rules take precedence. See the
[Student Manual, Part II, Sections F–G and J–L](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ew8hDsW_anZjLsZJKI3rEKAnhT1K4OTd/view)
and the
[Student Conduct, Discipline and Grievance Guidelines](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FA3IPniUsXfeqscEyS_FdN356I_EwxGm/view)
(BOR Resolution No. 34, series of 2022).

**Devices and notes**

- Phones and other personal electronic devices must be switched off and
  put away, including when consulting notes.
- If you have a device out or in use, you will be marked absent for that class.
- Approved accessibility arrangements and university-required exceptions
  take precedence.
- Use printed notes or, preferably, your own handwritten notes; bring
  paper and a pen or pencil.

**Participation and conduct**

- Difficulty understanding is not a reason for exclusion; ask for help.
- A clear and persistent unwillingness to engage will lead to being asked
  to step outside and return when ready to participate.
- Disruptive behaviour will be addressed under university disciplinary
  procedures. Participation marks follow the approved assessment criteria.

**Attendance and punctuality**

- Attend regularly. Arrival **15 minutes** after the start is recorded as
  tardy; arrival **20 minutes** after the start is recorded as absent.
- Being marked absent does not prevent attendance at the lesson.
- Before midterms, unexcused absences exceeding **20% of required semester
  contact hours** trigger automatic dropping, recorded as **FDA (failure due
  to absences) or UD (unofficially dropped)**.
- The absence total does not reset after midterms. These classifications
  are distinct from a numerical grade of 5.0.
- If absent, read the missed notes and attempt the problems before the
  next class; seek help promptly if needed.

**Excused absences**

Recognised grounds:

- Official university representation in curricular, co-curricular or
  extracurricular activities.
- Illness certified by your attending doctor or the University physician.
- *Force majeure*: unavoidable extraordinary events beyond your control.

Other absence rules:

- Weddings, parties and similar personal commitments do not qualify.
- Notify me promptly with supporting documentation and arrange to complete
  missed work.
- The handbook sets a **30% limit on excused absences**.

**Missed examinations**

- For an excused absence, contact me promptly with supporting documentation.
- Special examinations require the instructor's recommendation and unit
  head's approval under the manual's Section J.
- The final is **not automatically double-weighted**.
- An unexcused missed examination receives **zero**, subject to university rules.

**Marks and concerns**

- You may request an explanation or review of your marks and use the
  university grievance procedure.
- I may consider perfect attendance and meaningful participation when
  reviewing borderline marks, within university rules. Neither guarantees
  a pass or replaces required coursework.

**Commitment**

- Speak with me early if you anticipate difficulty meeting the requirements.
- If you cannot commit to preparation, attendance, participation and
  coursework, I recommend official withdrawal under university procedures
  and deadlines.

**Proofwriting and abstraction**

- This is a **proof-based course**.
- The aim is to reason precisely about objects, assumptions and relationships,
  as you would with code modules, interfaces and network configurations.
- You will practise explaining why a method works, justifying a claim and
  finding counterexamples.
